basics.name: Luna Lovegood
basics.label: Magizoologist, Field Naturalist & Investigative Journalist
basics.summary: Open-minded and exceptionally perceptive magizoologist with expertise in rare, disputed, and misclassified magical creatures. Contributor and assistant editor at The Quibbler, with a particular focus on cryptofaunal investigation and Wrackspurt phenomenology. Decorated member of Dumbledore's Army and veteran of the Battle of Hogwarts. Widely regarded as one of the most original thinkers in contemporary British wizarding natural philosophy. Comfortable operating in remote and hostile environments. Possesses an unusually high tolerance for social scepticism.

location.address: The Lovegood House, Ottery St Catchpole

work.name: Scamander & Lovegood Magizoological Research
work.summary: Conducts long-form field expeditions across five continents in partnership with husband Rolf Scamander (grandson of Newt Scamander) to document, classify, and advocate for the protection of rare and previously unrecognised magical species. Specialises in creatures that exist on the boundary between accepted taxonomy and cryptozoological speculation.
highlights: Co-discovered and formally documented the Blibbering Humdinger's summer migration corridor through the Scottish Highlands — overturning six decades of Ministry consensus that the creature was purely mythological
Produced the first photographic and pensieve-archived evidence of a living Crumple-Horned Snorkack in the wild, obtained during a three-month expedition to northern Sweden
Authored formal species protection applications for four newly documented creatures, successfully securing XXXXX-grade temporary preservation status for two
Developed a novel passive observation methodology using scent-neutralising charms and low-resonance Disillusionment spells that has been adopted by field magizoologists internationally

Led a successful campaign to reclassify the Nargle from 'unclassified' to 'Class II — Documented but Elusive', following the collection of seventeen independent herd observations in Welsh mistletoe groves
Trained ten junior wildlife researchers in field documentation, ethical capture-and-release protocols, and Nundu-adjacent safety procedures

work.name: The Quibbler
work.summary: Regular contributor and editorial collaborator at The Quibbler, the wizarding world's most independently-minded periodical. Responsible for cryptofaunal investigations, alternative healing spotlights, and Wrackspurt behavioural pattern reporting. Assisted in maintaining editorial independence during the publication's period of Ministry-hostile coverage.
highlights: Authored 'The Truth About Harry Potter', the first sympathetic and credible profile of Harry Potter's account of Voldemort's return, published at a time when the mainstream wizarding press refused to cover the story — a pivotal piece in shifting public opinion
Contributed the landmark 17-part series 'Creatures the Ministry Doesn't Want You to See', which attracted the publication's highest recorded readership
Maintained editorial operations during the period when editor Xenophilius Lovegood was held captive by Death Eaters, keeping four pending issues to press
Developed The Quibbler's first structured fact-checking process for creature sighting submissions, significantly improving the quality of field reports
Interviewed twelve survivors of the Battle of Hogwarts for the 1999 memorial issue, producing the most comprehensive first-hand account published in the wizarding press

work.name: Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry
work.position: Student Teaching Assistant — Care of Magical Creatures
work.summary: Volunteered as an informal assistant to Professor Grubbly-Plank and later Professor Hagrid in the Care of Magical Creatures class, providing supplementary context on creature behaviour drawn from independent reading and field observation.
highlights: Prepared supplementary illustrated lecture notes on Thestrals, including behavioural characteristics and care requirements, which were distributed to the class
One of only two students able to see and handle Thestrals from first year, providing crucial ground-level guidance to classmates experiencing their first encounter
Identified a misclassification in the class textbook's description of Knarl feeding habits and submitted a formal correction, later acknowledged by the publisher

volunteer.summary: One of the founding members of Dumbledore's Army secret Defence Against the Dark Arts training group. Participated in all training sessions and multiple direct combat engagements, including the Battle of the Department of Mysteries and the Battle of Hogwarts.
highlights: Participated in the Battle of the Department of Mysteries, fighting alongside Harry Potter and four other students against a squad of twelve Death Eaters — sustained minor injuries, continued fighting
Performed with exceptional composure and tactical effectiveness at the Battle of Hogwarts, defending multiple corridors alongside Ginny Weasley and Hermione Granger
Maintained the DA signal coins network during the 1997–98 academic year under Carrow-controlled Hogwarts, providing communication infrastructure for student resistance
Provided tactical intelligence on the Room of Requirement's layout and properties, facilitating its use as a refuge and staging area

volunteer.organization: Society for the Welfare of Magical Creatures (Unofficial)
volunteer.summary: Co-founded and ran an informal advocacy network pressing the Ministry's Beast Division to extend protections to cryptofaunal species pending formal classification.
highlights: Submitted twelve formal petitions to the Beast Division on behalf of disputed-status creatures
Organised the first 'Creatures in Limbo' symposium, attended by thirty-two magizoologists and Ministry officials
Secured provisional protected-habitat status for three nesting sites pending formal species review

awards.title: Order of Merlin, Third Class
awards.summary: Awarded for exceptional bravery and service during the Battle of Hogwarts and associated resistance operations against Voldemort's regime.

awards.title: Xenophilius Lovegood Award for Unconventional Journalism
awards.summary: Annual award recognising outstanding investigative journalism on under-reported subjects within the wizarding world. Awarded for the 'Creatures the Ministry Doesn't Want You to See' series.

awards.title: Ravenclaw Academic Commendation
awards.awarder: Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry
awards.summary: Awarded to graduating Ravenclaw students demonstrating exceptional independent scholarship over their academic career. Cited for original contributions to Care of Magical Creatures coursework.

certificates.issuer: International Confederation of Wizards — Creature Studies Committee

publications.name: The Truth About Harry Potter
publications.summary: Interview-based profile of Harry Potter presenting his first-hand account of Voldemort's return at the Triwizard Tournament. Published against significant mainstream press scepticism. Later recognised as the most accurate contemporaneous account of the Second Wizarding War's opening events.

publications.name: Nargles of the West: A Field Taxonomy
publications.summary: Peer-reviewed field study documenting seventeen independent Nargle colony observations in Welsh mistletoe groves, including habitat preferences, seasonal behaviour patterns, and interactions with neighbouring magical fauna. Led to the first formal reclassification of the Nargle in Ministry taxonomy.

publications.name: On the Wrackspurt and Its Influence on Cognitive Enchantment Susceptibility
publications.summary: Theoretical paper proposing a mechanism by which Wrackspurt infestation may correlate with increased susceptibility to certain classes of mind-affecting charms. Controversial within the mainstream magical academic community; cited extensively within independent research circles.

publications.name: Magical Creature Field Guide: Disputed and Misclassified Species (Vol. 1)
publications.summary: Co-authored with Rolf Scamander. A comprehensive reference work covering 41 creature species whose Ministry classification is disputed, unresolved, or based on outdated evidence. Includes original observational data from fourteen expeditions across eight countries.

references.name: Harry Potter, Auror & Order of the Phoenix Member
references.reference: Luna was one of the most loyal and dependable people I've ever known. In the Department of Mysteries, she kept her head when the rest of us were panicking, and she fought brilliantly. She has a way of seeing things that other people miss — I used to think it was just eccentric, but more often than not she turned out to be right. I'd trust her with my life, and I have done.

references.name: Rolf Scamander, Magizoologist & Co-Researcher
references.reference: In fourteen years of joint fieldwork, Luna has never once accepted a creature classification she hadn't personally verified. She has an almost uncanny ability to locate and observe creatures without distressing them, and her attention to the nuances of animal behaviour exceeds anyone else I've worked with. The Blibbering Humdinger discovery alone would have secured her place in the field — the Snorkack evidence will, when the academic community catches up, be considered one of the great finds of the century.

references.name: Xenophilius Lovegood, Editor — The Quibbler
references.reference: Luna has inherited my absolute commitment to printing the truth as it is, not as people wish it to be. The Potter article required courage I sometimes doubted I possessed, but she never wavered. She will go further than I ever did. She already has.

projects.name: Operation Snorkack — Northern Sweden Expedition
projects.description: A three-month solo field expedition to northern Sweden to document the habitat and behavioural patterns of the Crumple-Horned Snorkack. Utilised a proprietary passive observation platform and a novel sympathetic-magic tracking system developed over two years of preparation.
highlights: Obtained the first verified photographic and pensieve-archived evidence of a living Crumple-Horned Snorkack
Mapped a 40-square-kilometre habitat range and documented seventeen discrete behavioural observations
Submitted formal evidence package to the Ministry's Beast Division; review ongoing
Survived an unexpected confrontation with a territorial Erkling in week six with no lasting injuries

projects.name: The Nargle Reclassification Project
projects.description: Systematic multi-site field study of Nargle colony behaviour in Welsh mistletoe groves, designed to provide sufficient evidence for a formal Ministry reclassification from 'unclassified' to 'documented species'.
highlights: Identified seventeen distinct colony sites across eight counties
Documented seasonal behaviour patterns, nesting habits, and Nargle-mistletoe symbiotic relationship
Successfully petitioned for reclassification — the first new creature formally added to the Ministry's Class II list in eleven years
Peer-reviewed publication in the Journal of Magical Natural History cited 43 times within five years
